correctness.rationale: Diamond subgraphs are confined to row or column cliques. The row K_n gives a lower bound binomial(n,2) for n>=4. A perfect matching of the regular bipartite Kneser disjointness relation gives a permutation psi sending each 2-subset to a disjoint 2-subset. Translation-based row and column colour assignments are separately injective, and disjointness of psi prevents all cross-orientation incidents from sharing a colour. Restriction from the n-by-n graph proves all rectangles. The three n<=3 cases are certified by direct proper colourings and the 18>4*4 matching-size obstruction. Standalone Python checks verify 33 larger cases and three small ones; these tests are not claimed to prove the infinite result.

value.rationale: Determines a newly introduced natural invariant on all two-dimensional rook/Hamming graphs, with an unexpected sharp equality to one row-clique lower bound despite the intersections with column cliques. The perfect-matching design is a reusable structural construction and gives explicit finite-time optimum colourings. It goes materially beyond classical edge-colouring and general degree bounds; its scope is mathematically natural rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
